Q 15:88–89 · Vol. 2, pp. 588–589

Verses 88 to 89

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given certain categories of them to enjoy, and do not grieve over them, and lower your wing to the believers (88), and say: Indeed I am the clear warner (89)
لا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَاخْفِضْ جَناحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (88) وَقُلْ إِنِّي أَنَا النَّذِيرُ الْمُبِينُ (89)
Vol. 2, p. 588
. That is: do not look with an aspiring gaze, desiring it and longing for it, toward what We have given "certain categories of them" — kinds of the disbelievers.
أى: لا تطمح ببصرك طموح راغب فيه متمنّ له إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ أصنافاً من الكفار.
Question
If you say: how does this connect with what precedes it? [1]
فإن قلت: كيف وصل هذا بما قبله؟ «1»
Answer
I say: He says to the Messenger of God ﷺ: you have been given the greatest blessing, compared with which every blessing, however great, is insignificant and tiny, namely the great Qur'an; so you must be content with it, and "do not extend your eyes" toward the enjoyments of the world. Of this is the ḥadīth: "He is not of us who does not [become self-sufficient/chant melodiously] with the Qur'an" [2], and the ḥadīth of Abū Bakr: "Whoever is given the Qur'an and sees that anyone has been given better of the world than what he was given has belittled something great and magnified something small" [3]. It is also said: there arrived from Buṣrā and Adhriʿāt seven caravans for the Jews
قلت: يقول لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قد أوتيت النعمة العظمى التي كل نعمة وإن عظمت فهي إليها حقيرة ضئيلة، وهي القرآن العظيم، فعليك أن تستغني به، ولا تمدّن عينيك إلى متاع الدنيا. ومنه الحديث «ليس منا من لم يتغنّ بالقرآن، «2» وحديث أبى بكر «من أوتى القرآن فرأى أن أحداً أوتى من الدنيا أفضل مما أوتى، فقد صغر عظيما وعظم صغيراً «3» » وقيل: وافت من بصرى وأذرعات: سبع قوافل ليهود
Vol. 2, p. 589
of Banū Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr, carrying kinds of fine cloth, perfume, jewels and all sorts of goods; the Muslims said: if these goods were ours we would strengthen ourselves with them and spend them in the way of God. So God Almighty and Exalted said to them: I have given you seven verses which are better than these seven caravans. "and do not grieve over them": i.e. do not covet their wealth, and do not grieve over them that they did not believe so that Islam would be strengthened by their position and the believers revived through them; but be humble toward those with you of the poor and weak among the believers, and set your soul at ease about the faith of the rich and the strong. "and say to them: Indeed I am the clear warner": I warn you, with clarity and proof, that God's punishment is descending upon you.
بنى قريظة والنضير، فيها أنواع البز والطيب والجوهر وسائر الأمتعة، فقال المسلمون: لو كانت هذه الأموال لنا لتقوّينا بها، ولأنفقناها في سبيل الله، فقال لهم الله عز وعلا: لقد أعطيتكم سبع آيات هي خير من هذه القوافل السبع وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ أى لا تتمنّ أموالهم ولا تحزن عليهم أنهم لم يؤمنوا فيتقوّى بمكانهم الإسلام وينتعش بهم المؤمنون، وتواضع لمن معك من فقراء المؤمنين وضعفائهم، وطب نفساً عن إيمان الأغنياء والأقوياء وَقُلْ لهم إِنِّي أَنَا النَّذِيرُ الْمُبِينُ أنذركم ببيان وبرهان أنّ عذاب الله نازل بكم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 588
1. (1). Maḥmūd said: "If you say: how does this connect with what precedes it … etc." Aḥmad said: This is the correct meaning of the ḥadīth; many scholars took it to mean singing (ghināʾ) and claimed that "taghannā" is formed only from the lengthened "ghināʾ" [singing] and not from the shortened "ghinā" [self-sufficiency], and that its verb is "istaghnā" in particular. But I found the formation of "taghannā" from the shortened "ghinā" in the sound ḥadīth about horses: "As for the one that is a covering, it is a man who tied it for self-sufficiency (taghanniyan) and chastity" — and this is definitely and by agreement from the shortened "ghinā," and is a verbal noun of "taghannā," so that indicates it is used from both formations, contrary to the claim of the opponent. God is the Grantor of success. 2. Narrated by al-Bukhārī from the route of Abū Salama from Abū Hurayra, and on the topic there is [a report] from Saʿd and Abū Lubāba in Abū Dāwūd. The one who traced it said: al-Nawawī, and before him al-Mundhirī, then al-Ṭībī, overlooked it, attributing it to Abū Dāwūd and not attributing it to al-Bukhārī; and al-Qurṭubī erred, attributing it to Muslim and not to al-Bukhārī; and the author of Jāmiʿ al-Uṣūl did not mention it; and al-Ḥākim attributed it to the two Shaykhs, whereas what is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs is the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra: "God does not listen to anything as He listens to a prophet who chants the Qur'an melodiously, reciting it aloud." A benefit: al-Bayhaqī said in al-Sunan in the Book of Testimonies: al-Ḥākim informed us from Abū al-Aṣamm: I heard al-Rabīʿ say: I heard al-Shāfiʿī say: "He is not of us who does not taghanna with the Qur'an." A man said to him: [Does it mean] become self-sufficient? He said: That is not its meaning; its meaning is that he recites it with a mournful tone. 3. I did not find it from Abū Bakr; Ibn ʿAdī narrated it in the biography of Ḥamza al-Naṣībī from Zayd ibn Rufayʿ from Abū ʿUbayda from Ibn Masʿūd, raising it to the Prophet: "Whoever learns the Qur'an and thinks that anyone is richer than he has belittled something great and magnified something small." Ḥamza was accused of fabrication. Isḥāq and al-Ṭabarī narrated it from the ḥadīth of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar in these words: "Whoever is given the Qur'an and sees that anyone has been given better than what he was given has magnified what God made small and belittled what God made great — the ḥadīth."

Q 15:90–91 · Vol. 2, pp. 589–590

Verses 90 to 91

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Just as We sent down upon the dividers (90), who made the Qur'an into parts (91)
كَما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَى الْمُقْتَسِمِينَ (90) الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا الْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ (91)
Vol. 2, p. 589
.
Question
If you say: to what is "just as We sent down" connected?
فإن قلت: بم تعلق قوله كَما أَنْزَلْنا؟
Answer
I say: there are two aspects. One: that it is connected to His words "And We have certainly given you" — i.e., We sent down upon you the like of what We sent down upon the People of the Book, who are "the dividers" — "who made the Qur'an into parts," in that they said, out of their obstinacy and hostility, that part of it is true, in agreement with the Torah and the Gospel, and part of it false, in contradiction to them; so they divided it into truth and falsehood, and cut it up (ʿaḍḍawhu) [1]. It is also said: they used to mock it, so one of them would say: Sūrat al-Baqara is mine, and another would say: Sūrat Āl ʿImrān is mine. It is also possible that "Qur'an" means what they recite of their own books, which they divided by their distortion, in that the Jews acknowledged part of the Torah and denied part, and the Christians acknowledged part of the Gospel and denied part; and this is a consolation to the Messenger of God ﷺ for what his people did with the Qur'an and their denial of it, and their saying: sorcery, poetry, tales of the ancients — that others among the disbelievers did the like of what they did to other books. The second: that it is connected to His words "and say: Indeed I am the clear warner" — i.e. and warn Quraysh of the like of the punishment We sent down upon the dividers, meaning the Jews, which is what befell Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr, treating the anticipated as if it had occurred, which is part of inimitability, because it is a report of what would happen, and it has happened. It is also possible that "those who made the Qur'an into parts" is accusative as the object of "the warner," i.e. warn those who cut it up, who divide the Qur'an into sorcery, poetry and tales of the ancients, like what We sent down upon the dividers, and they are the twelve who divided the entrances of Mecca in the days of the season, so they sat at each entrance separately to turn people away from believing in the Messenger of God ﷺ; one of them would say: Do not be deceived by the one who goes out from among us, for he is a sorcerer; another: a liar; another: a poet. So God destroyed them at the Day of Badr and before it with afflictions, such as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra,
قلت: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يتعلق بقوله: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْناكَ أى أنزلنا عليك مثل ما أنزلنا على أهل الكتاب وهم المقتسمون الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا الْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ حيث قالوا بعنادهم وعدوانهم بعضه حق موافق للتوراة والإنجيل، وبعضه باطل مخالف لهما، فاقتسموه إلى حق وباطل، وعضوه «1» . وقيل: كانوا يستهزؤن به فيقول بعضهم: سورة البقرة لي، ويقول الآخر: سورة آل عمران لي. ويجوز أن يراد بالقرآن: ما يقرءونه من كتبهم، وقد اقتسموه بتحريفهم، وبأنّ اليهود أقرّت ببعض التوراة وكذبت ببعض، والنصارى أقرت ببعض الإنجيل وكذبت ببعض، وهذه تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صنيع قومه بالقرآن وتكذيبهم، وقولهم سحر وشعر وأساطير، بأن غيرهم من الكفرة فعلوا بغيره من الكتب نحو فعلهم. والثاني أن يتعلق بقوله: وَقُلْ إِنِّي أَنَا النَّذِيرُ الْمُبِينُ أى: وأنذر قريشاً مثل ما أنزلنا من العذاب على المقتسمين، يعنى اليهود، وهو ما جرى على قريظة والنضير، جعل المتوقع بمنزلة الواقع، وهو من الإعجاز، لأنه إخبار بما سيكون وقد كان. ويجوز أن يكون الذين جعلوا القرآن عضين منصوباً بالنذير، أى: أنذر المعضين الذين يجزءون القرآن إلى سحر وشعر وأساطير، مثل ما أنزلنا على المقتسمين وهم الاثنا عشر الذين اقتسموا مداخل مكة أيام الموسم، فقعدوا في كل مدخل متفرّقين لينفروا الناس عن الإيمان برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، يقول بعضهم: لا تغتروا بالخارج منا فإنه ساحر. ويقول الآخر: كذاب، والآخر: شاعر، فأهلكهم الله يوم بدر وقبله بآفات، كالوليد بن المغيرة،
Vol. 2, p. 590
and al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib and others; or like what We sent down upon the band who swore to attack Ṣāliḥ ﷺ by night; and "iqtisām" is in the sense of "taqāsum."
والعاص بن وائل، والأسود بن المطلب وغيرهم، أو مثل ما أنزلنا على الرهط الذين تقاسموا على أن يبيتوا صالحاً عليه السلام، والاقتسام بمعنى التقاسم.
Question
If you say: if you connect His words "just as We sent down" to "And We have certainly given you," what is the meaning of the interposing of "Do not extend your eyes" up to the end between them?
فإن قلت: إذا علقت قوله: كَما أَنْزَلْنا بقوله: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْناكَ فما معنى توسط لا تَمُدَّنَّ إلى آخره بينهما؟
Answer
I say: since that was a consolation for the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning their denial and enmity, what was an aid to the meaning of consolation was interposed — the prohibition from looking toward their worldly goods and from grieving over their disbelief, and the command that he turn with all his being toward the believers. "ʿiḍīn": parts, plural of "ʿiḍa," whose origin is "ʿiḍwa," a form fiʿla from "ʿaḍā al-shāt" when one made it limbs. Ruʾba said: "And the religion of God is not cut up" [wa-laysa dīnu llāhi bi-l-maʿḍiyy]. It is also said that it is fiʿla from "ʿaḍahtuhu" when I slandered him [1]. From ʿIkrima: "al-ʿiḍa" is sorcery in the language of Quraysh; they call a sorceress "ʿāḍiha." And the Prophet ﷺ cursed the "ʿāḍiha" and the "mustaʿḍiha" [2]; its deficiency is a wāw on the first view and a hāʾ on the second.
قلت: لما كان ذلك تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن تكذيبهم وعداوتهم، اعترض بما هو مدد لمعنى التسلية. من النهى عن الالتفات إلى دنياهم والتأسف على كفرهم، ومن الأمر بأن يقبل بمجامعه على المؤمنين عِضِينَ أجزاء، جمع عضة، وأصلها عضوة فعلة من عضى الشاة إذا جعلها أعضاء. قال رؤبة: وَلَيْسَ دِينُ اللَّهِ بِالْمَعْضِىِ وقيل: هي فعلة، من عضهته إذا بهته «1» . وعن عكرمة: العضة السحر، بلغة قريش، يقولون للساحرة عاضهة. ولعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم العاضهة «2» والمستعضهة، نقصانها على الأوّل واو، وعلى الثاني هاء.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 589
1. (1). His word "wa-ʿaḍḍawhu": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "ʿaḍḍaytu al-shāt taʿḍiyatan" when I divided it into limbs; and "ʿaḍḍaytu al-shayʾ taʿḍiyatan" when I separated it. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «وعضوه» في الصحاح: عضيت الشاة تعضية، إذا جزأتها أعضاء. وعضيت الشيء تعضية، إذا فرقته. (ع)
Vol. 2, p. 590
1. (1). His words "when I slandered him": i.e. accused him. (ʿ) 2. Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā and Ibn ʿAdī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās. In its chain are Zamʿa ibn Ṣāliḥ from Salama ibn Wahrām, and both are weak. It has a corroboration in ʿAbd al-Razzāq from a narration of Ibn Jurayj from ʿAṭāʾ. 3. "So he said to me the words of one of insight and ability, … a pure, free one, free of doubt: I commanded you the good, so do what you were commanded [with it], … for I have left you with wealth and property (nashab)." By Khufāf ibn Nudba; it is also said, by al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās; it is also said, by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib; it is also said, by Iyās ibn Mūsā. "Al-maqdira" [may be read] with the three vowels on the dāl: power; "al-muḥarrar al-nazih" — like "ḥadhir" — means pure of deceit; "al-rayb" means doubt, and it is an attribute of "dhī raʾy"; had you made it an attribute of "raʾy," there would be a separation between the attribute and the described by a coordinating conjunction. Its rafʿ is also permissible as a cut-off attribute of "al-qawl." "Al-nashab": the original property, silent or speaking, so it is coordination of the specific with the general. It is also narrated "dhā nasab" with the unpointed sīn: i.e. a great lineage; and "amara" is transitive to the second object with "bi-"; and "I commanded you the good" is said by extension, or by way of including the sense of "assigning," and the poet combined them in the line.
1. (1) . قوله «إذا بهته» أى اتهمته. (ع)
2. . أخرجه أبو يعلى وابن عدى من حديث ابن عباس. وفي إسناده زمعة بن صالح عن سلمة بن وهرام، وهما ضعيفان. وله شاهد عند عبد الرزاق من رواية عن ابن جريج عن عطاء.
3. . فقال لي قول ذى رأى ومقدرة
…. محرر نزه خال من الريب أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به
…. فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب لخفاف بن ندبة، وقيل: لعباس بن مرداس. وقيل: لعمرو بن معديكرب. وقيل: لا ياس بن موسى، والمقدرة: مثلث الدال: القوة، والمحرر النزه- كحذر-: الخالص من الغش. والريب، أى الشبه، وهو نعت لذي رأى. ولو جعلته نعتا للرأى لكان فيه الفصل بين النعت والمنعوت بالعطف. ويجوز رفعه على أنه نعت مقطوع للقول. والنشب: المال الأصل صامتا أو ناطقا، فهو من عطف الخاص على العام. ويروى: ذا نسب، بالمهملة: أى نسب عظيم، وأمر: يتعدى للثاني بالباء. ويقال: أمرتك الخير على التوسع، أو تضمين التكليف، وجمعهما الشاعر في البيت.
31
Q 15:92–93 · Vol. 2, p. 590

Verses 92 to 93

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So by your Lord, We will surely question them all (92), about what they used to do (93)
فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَسْئَلَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (92) عَمَّا كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (93)
Vol. 2, p. 590
. "We will surely question them" is an expression for the threat. It is also said: He will question them with a questioning of reproach. From Abū al-ʿĀliya: servants will be asked about two things: what they used to worship, and what they answered the messengers.
لَنَسْئَلَنَّهُمْ عبارة عن الوعيد. وقيل. يسألهم سؤال تقريع. وعن أبى العالية: يسأل العباد عن خلتين: عما كانوا يعبدون، وماذا أجابوا المرسلين.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 590
1. (1). His words "when I slandered him": i.e. accused him. (ʿ) 2. Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā and Ibn ʿAdī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās. In its chain are Zamʿa ibn Ṣāliḥ from Salama ibn Wahrām, and both are weak. It has a corroboration in ʿAbd al-Razzāq from a narration of Ibn Jurayj from ʿAṭāʾ. 3. "So he said to me the words of one of insight and ability, … a pure, free one, free of doubt: I commanded you the good, so do what you were commanded [with it], … for I have left you with wealth and property (nashab)." By Khufāf ibn Nudba; it is also said, by al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās; it is also said, by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib; it is also said, by Iyās ibn Mūsā. "Al-maqdira" [may be read] with the three vowels on the dāl: power; "al-muḥarrar al-nazih" — like "ḥadhir" — means pure of deceit; "al-rayb" means doubt, and it is an attribute of "dhī raʾy"; had you made it an attribute of "raʾy," there would be a separation between the attribute and the described by a coordinating conjunction. Its rafʿ is also permissible as a cut-off attribute of "al-qawl." "Al-nashab": the original property, silent or speaking, so it is coordination of the specific with the general. It is also narrated "dhā nasab" with the unpointed sīn: i.e. a great lineage; and "amara" is transitive to the second object with "bi-"; and "I commanded you the good" is said by extension, or by way of including the sense of "assigning," and the poet combined them in the line.
1. (1) . قوله «إذا بهته» أى اتهمته. (ع)
2. . أخرجه أبو يعلى وابن عدى من حديث ابن عباس. وفي إسناده زمعة بن صالح عن سلمة بن وهرام، وهما ضعيفان. وله شاهد عند عبد الرزاق من رواية عن ابن جريج عن عطاء.
3. . فقال لي قول ذى رأى ومقدرة

…. فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب لخفاف بن ندبة، وقيل: لعباس بن مرداس. وقيل: لعمرو بن معديكرب. وقيل: لا ياس بن موسى، والمقدرة: مثلث الدال: القوة، والمحرر النزه- كحذر-: الخالص من الغش. والريب، أى الشبه، وهو نعت لذي رأى. ولو جعلته نعتا للرأى لكان فيه الفصل بين النعت والمنعوت بالعطف. ويجوز رفعه على أنه نعت مقطوع للقول. والنشب: المال الأصل صامتا أو ناطقا، فهو من عطف الخاص على العام. ويروى: ذا نسب، بالمهملة: أى نسب عظيم، وأمر: يتعدى للثاني بالباء. ويقال: أمرتك الخير على التوسع، أو تضمين التكليف، وجمعهما الشاعر في البيت.
32
Q 15:94 · Vol. 2, pp. 590–591

Verse 94

The verse as the commentary quotes it
So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists (94)
فَاصْدَعْ بِما تُؤْمَرُ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (94)
Vol. 2, p. 590
. "So proclaim what you are commanded": make it public and make it manifest. One says: "ṣadaʿa bi-l-ḥujja" when he spoke it openly, as in your saying "ṣarraḥa bihā," from "ṣadīʿ," which is the dawn; and "ṣadʿ" in glass is clear separation. It is also said: "fa-iṣdaʿ" — separate between truth and falsehood by what you are commanded; and the meaning: by what you are commanded of the laws, so the preposition was omitted, as in the saying: "I commanded you the good, so do what you were commanded [with it]" [3]
فَاصْدَعْ بِما تُؤْمَرُ فاجهر به وأظهره. يقال: صدع بالحجة إذا تكلم بها جهاراً، كقولك: صرح بها، من الصديع وهو الفجر، والصدع في الزجاجة: الإبانة. وقيل: فَاصْدَعْ فافرق بين الحق والباطل بما تؤمر، والمعنى: بما تؤمر به من الشرائع فحذف الجارّ، كقوله: أَمَرْتُكَ الْخَيْرَ فَافْعَلْ مَا أُمِرْتَ بِهِ «3»
Vol. 2, p. 591
It is also possible that "bi-mā" is a verbal-noun particle, i.e. "by your command," a verbal noun from the passive.
ويجوز أن تكون بِما مصدرية، أى بأمرك مصدر من المبنى للمفعول.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 590
1. (1). His words "when I slandered him": i.e. accused him. (ʿ) 2. Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā and Ibn ʿAdī from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās. 2. . أخرجه أبو يعلى وابن عدى من حديث ابن عباس. وفي إسناده زمعة بن صالح عن سلمة بن وهرام، وهما ضعيفان. وله شاهد عند عبد الرزاق من رواية عن ابن جريج عن عطاء.

…. محرر نزه خال من الريب أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به
…. فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب لخفاف بن ندبة، وقيل: لعباس بن مرداس. وقيل: لعمرو بن معديكرب. وقيل: لا ياس بن موسى، والمقدرة: مثلث الدال: القوة، والمحرر النزه- كحذر-: الخالص من الغش. والريب، أى الشبه، وهو نعت لذي رأى. ولو جعلته نعتا للرأى لكان فيه الفصل بين النعت والمنعوت بالعطف. ويجوز رفعه على أنه نعت مقطوع للقول. والنشب: المال الأصل صامتا أو ناطقا، فهو من عطف الخاص على العام. ويروى: ذا نسب، بالمهملة: أى نسب عظيم، وأمر: يتعدى للثاني بالباء. ويقال: أمرتك الخير على التوسع، أو تضمين التكليف، وجمعهما الشاعر في البيت.
Vol. 2, p. 591
1. (1). I did not find it in this wording. Al-Ṭabarānī narrated it in his two Muʿjams, and Abū Nuʿaym and al-Bayhaqī in their Dalāʾil, and Ibn Mardawayh, all of them from the route of Jaʿfar ibn Iyās from Saʿīd from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the words of God the Exalted "Indeed We have sufficed you against the mockers." He said: They are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, Abū Zamʿa and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyṭal al-Sahmī. He said: Gabriel came to him and he complained of them to him. He showed him al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, and Gabriel pointed to his akḥal [arm vein]. He said: What did you do? He said: I sufficed you against him. And he related the ḥadīth. He said: As for al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, he passed by a man of Khuzāʿa who was feathering an arrow of his, and it hit his akḥal and cut it. As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, he went blind. As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, boils broke out on his head and he died of them. As for al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, he rode to al-Ṭāʾif and tethered his donkey to a shibraqa, meaning a thorn; it entered the sole of his foot and killed him. As for al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyṭal, he was seized by the yellow-ailment in his belly until his excrement came out of his mouth and he died of it.
1. (1) . لم أجده بهذا السياق. وأخرجه الطبراني في معجميه. وأبو نعيم والبيهقي في الدلائل لهما. وابن مردويه كلهم من طريق جعفر بن إياس عن سعيد عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى إِنَّا كَفَيْناكَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ قال: هم الوليد بن المغيرة والعاص بن وائل والأسود بن عبد يغوث والأسود بن المطلب وأبو زمعة والحرث بن عيطل السهمي قال أتاه جبريل فشكاهم إليه. فأراه الوليد بن المغيرة فأومأ جبريل إلى أكحله. فقال: ما صنعت؟ قال: كفيته. فساق الحديث. قال: فأما الوليد بن المغيرة فمر برجل من خزاعة وهو يريش نبلا له فأصاب أكحله فقطعها. وأما الأسود ابن المطلب فعمى. وأما الأسود بن عبد يغوث فخرج في رأسه قروح فمات منها، وأما العاص بن وائل فركب إلى الطائف فربط به حماره على شبرقة يعنى شوكة. فدخلت في أخمص قدمه فقتلته. وأما الحرث بن عيطل فأخذه ألم الأصفر في بطنه حتى خرج خرءه من فيه فمات منها»
33
Q 15:95–96 · Vol. 2, p. 591

Verses 95 to 96

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Indeed We have sufficed you against the mockers (95), those who make with God another god; but they will soon know (96)
إِنَّا كَفَيْناكَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ (95) الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ (96)
Vol. 2, p. 591
. From ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr concerning the mockers: they are five persons of age and standing: al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, and al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṭalāṭila. From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ: they all died before Badr. Gabriel ﷺ said to the Prophet ﷺ: I have been commanded to suffice you against them. He pointed to the shin of al-Walīd; he passed by arrow-makers and an arrow caught on his garment, and he did not turn, thinking it beneath him to pick it up, so it struck a vein in his heel and cut it, and he died. He pointed to the sole of the foot of al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and a thorn entered it; he said: I am stung, I am stung; and his foot swelled until it became like a millstone, and he died. He pointed to the eyes of al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib and he went blind. He pointed to the nose of al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, and he blew out pus from his nose and died. And [he pointed] to al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth while he was sitting at the foot of a tree, and he began butting his head against the tree and striking his face on thorns until he died [1].
عن عروة بن الزبير في المستهزئين: هم خمسة نفر ذوو أسنان وشرف: الوليد بن المغيرة، والعاص بن وائل، والأسود بن عبد يغوث، والأسود بن المطلب، والحرث بن الطلاطلة. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: ماتوا كلهم قبل بدر. قال جبريل عليه السلام للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أمرت أن أكفيكهم، فأومأ إلى ساق الوليد فمرّ بنبال فتعلق بثوبه سهم، فلم ينعطف تعظماً لأخذه، فأصاب عرقاً في عقبه فقطعه فمات، وأومأ إلى أحمص العاص بن وائل، فدخلت فيها شوكة، فقال: لدغت لدغت وانتفخت رجله، حتى صارت كالرحى ومات، وأشار إلى عينى الأسود بن المطلب، فعمى وأشار إلى أنف الحرث بن قيس، فامتخط قيحاً فمات، وإلى الأسود بن عبد يغوث وهو قاعد في أصل شجرة، فجعل ينطح رأسه بالشجرة ويضرب وجهه بالشوك حتى مات «1» .
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 2, p. 591

Q 15:97–99 · Vol. 2, pp. 591–592

Verses 97 to 99

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say (97). So exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and be among the prostrators (98), and worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty (99)
وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ بِما يَقُولُونَ (97) فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ (98) وَاعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ (99)
Vol. 2, p. 591
. "by what they say": of the sayings of those who slander you and the Qur'an. "so exalt": so take refuge in what befalls you with God. And taking refuge with God is constant remembrance and much prostration; it will suffice you and lift grief from you. And persist
بِما يَقُولُونَ من أقاويل الطاعنين فيك وفي القرآن فَسَبِّحْ فافزع فيما نابك إلى الله. والفزع إلى الله: هو الذكر الدائم وكثرة السجود، يكفك ويكشف عنك الغم. ودم
Vol. 2, p. 592
in worshipping your Lord "until there comes to you the certainty," that is, death; i.e., as long as you live do not neglect worship. It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that whenever a matter distressed him he would take refuge in prayer [1]. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Ḥijr will have ten good deeds as reward, in the number of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and of the mockers of Muhammad ﷺ" [2].
على عبادة ربك حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ أى الموت، أى ما دمت حياً فلا تخل بالعبادة. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه كان إذا حزبه أمر فزع إلى الصلاة «1» . عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة الحجر كان له من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد المهاجرين والأنصار، والمستهزئين بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم» «2»
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 2, p. 591
1. (1). I did not find it in this wording. Al-Ṭabarānī narrated it in his two Muʿjams, and Abū Nuʿaym and al-Bayhaqī in their Dalāʾil, and Ibn Mardawayh, all of them from the route of Jaʿfar ibn Iyās from Saʿīd from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the words of God the Exalted "Indeed We have sufficed you against the mockers." He said: They are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, Abū Zamʿa and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyṭal al-Sahmī. He said: Gabriel came to him and he complained of them to him. He showed him al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, and Gabriel pointed to his akḥal [arm vein]. He said: What did you do? He said: I sufficed you against him. And he related the ḥadīth. He said: As for al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, he passed by a man of Khuzāʿa who was feathering an arrow of his, and it hit his akḥal and cut it. As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, he went blind. As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, boils broke out on his head and he died of them. As for al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, he rode to al-Ṭāʾif and tethered his donkey to a shibraqa, meaning a thorn; it entered the sole of his foot and killed him. As for al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyṭal, he was seized by the yellow-ailment in his belly until his excrement came out of his mouth and he died of it.
1. (1) . لم أجده بهذا السياق. وأخرجه الطبراني في معجميه. وأبو نعيم والبيهقي في الدلائل لهما. وابن مردويه كلهم من طريق جعفر بن إياس عن سعيد عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى إِنَّا كَفَيْناكَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ قال: هم الوليد بن المغيرة والعاص بن وائل والأسود بن عبد يغوث والأسود بن المطلب وأبو زمعة والحرث بن عيطل السهمي قال أتاه جبريل فشكاهم إليه. فأراه الوليد بن المغيرة فأومأ جبريل إلى أكحله. فقال: ما صنعت؟ قال: كفيته. فساق الحديث. قال: فأما الوليد بن المغيرة فمر برجل من خزاعة وهو يريش نبلا له فأصاب أكحله فقطعها. وأما الأسود ابن المطلب فعمى. وأما الأسود بن عبد يغوث فخرج في رأسه قروح فمات منها، وأما العاص بن وائل فركب إلى الطائف فربط به حماره على شبرقة يعنى شوكة. فدخلت في أخمص قدمه فقتلته. وأما الحرث بن عيطل فأخذه ألم الأصفر في بطنه حتى خرج خرءه من فيه فمات منها»
Vol. 2, p. 592
1. (1). It has preceded in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. 2. Narrated by al-Thaʿlabī from the route of Abū al-Khalīl from ʿAlī ibn Zayd from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Its chains of transmission have preceded at the end of Āl ʿImrān.
1. (1) . تقدم في البقرة.
2. . رواه الثعلبي من طريق أبى الخليل عن على بن زيد عن زر بن حبيش عن أبى بن كعب. وقد تقدمت أسانيده في آخر آل عمران.
